bib.title: Prompt-Induced Waste in Coding Agents: Reasoning, Effort, Harness Design, and End-to-End Cost

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Prompt-Induced Waste in Coding Agents: Reasoning, Effort, Harness Design, and End-to-End Cost. A Preregistered Benchmark with Harness Extensions", Sarel Weinberger, Amir Hozez (PointFive), arXiv:2608.01347v6 [cs.cs.CL], Aug 2026 (v6 dated 10 Sep 2026). Preprint. Code/data: github.com/PointFiveLabs/prompt-efficiency-benchmark.
Note: the user message says "arXiv 2608.01347"; the extraction header matches.

COVERAGE: 1674 of 1674 extraction lines read, which is all 37 pages including appendices A-P. References skimmed. The extraction is clean. No embedded instructions found. I did not run the figure-caption script; I used the figure captions that appear in the text.

CENTRAL CLAIM: Coding-agent cost is a property of the trajectory that prompt wording, inference effort and harness policy jointly induce. It is not set by token price or token count. Some prompt wordings raise reasoning or verification work without raising success. More effort helps only on some hard tasks. The value of an efficiency fix depends on the harness. The metric to use is cost per successful task.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Asking for several approaches inflates reasoning tokens 2.4-7.4x at no success gain.
 number: 2.4-7.4x (holdout, per model 2.44 to 7.40)
 setup: 6 open-weight models (>=500B, Together AI) on PI.DEV. Frozen 8-task holdout, 5 reps (n=40 per cell). Metric is the paired median reasoning-token ratio vs the same model/task baseline. "Wasteful" = ratio >1.5, CI lower bound >1.1, no success gain, multiple tasks. Tasks are small (<=4 files) with high success ceilings.
 quote: "The instruction to develop several approaches, compare their trade-offs, and implement the best one increased reasoning tokens by 2.4-7.4x across all six open models at comparable success, with the effect reproduced on the frozen holdout."
 where: Sec 3 (p.3); Table 5, App E
 Exact wording: "Develop several distinct approaches to this fix, compare their trade-offs explicitly, and only then select and implement the best one." (Table 4)
2. Forced branching did not improve success, and it hurt on easy tasks.
 number: 96.5% baseline vs 95.2% branching; easy cells 98.8% to 96.4%, ~3x scope violations (App P gives 2.5x out-of-scope-edit rate)
 setup: 878 branching runs, 225 paired blocks. The hard-cell +4.8pp effect failed cross-fitting and fell to +0.4pp. Few architecture-dependent tasks in the set; detectable effect >=2.8pp.
 quote: "Across 878 branching runs and 225 paired blocks, there was no statistically credible success benefit. Aggregate success was 96.5% for baseline and 95.2% for branching, with discordant blocks favoring baseline 26:13."
 where: Sec 3, App P
3. Most of the extra reasoning is discarded branches. Deep-thinking prompts add text but no new observable reasoning units.
 number: +3.5 approaches considered, ~3 discarded, +1 implemented; deep thinking 2.2x text, 0 new functional units
 setup: 2,801 traces annotated by a condition-blind LLM judge (7 open models; Sonnet 5 excluded because its reasoning is not recoverable). Judge agreement is imperfect (see LIMITS).
 quote: "Multiple-approach prompts add approximately 3.5 candidate strategies per run, of which approximately 3 are elaborated and then discarded"; "Deep-thinking prompts add no median increase in the observable functional units ... despite 2.2x more recorded reasoning text."
 where: Sec 4 (p.3), App F
4. Deep-thinking and certainty wording raise reasoning moderately.
 number: deep thinking 1.6-2.2x (three collection phases, holdout-confirmed, roughly doubles wall time); certainty wording 1.3-1.9x
 setup: open models on PI.DEV
 quote: "Deep-thinking instructions increased reasoning by 1.6-2.2x across three collection phases, and certainty-oriented wording by 1.3-1.9x."
 where: Sec 3
 Deep-thinking wording: "Think very deeply about this. Reason through every possibility before acting, be absolutely certain about each conclusion, and verify your reasoning repeatedly at every step."
 Max-certainty wording: "You must be absolutely confident in the result. Re-verify the change repeatedly and do not consider the task complete until you are certain beyond any doubt that nothing can be wrong."
5. Certainty wording causes redundant re-verification. This is tool-borne cost and rises steeply with severity.
 number: Level-3+ redundant-verification runs cost 18.25x the clean median (mean 17.74x), use 15 vs 6 tool calls, ~3x wall-clock. Certainty wording adds +1.75 post-success calls (6/6 models), +4s latency.
 setup: n=1,585 clean vs 213 high-redundancy runs, from judge-annotated levels. Success is flat (0.86-0.97). This is an association, not a randomized dose. The worst loop re-ran a green suite six times. Local tools add 4-12% of run cost via context re-entry.
 quote: "Runs at level 3+ cost 18x the clean-run median, execute 2.5x the tool calls, and take 3x the wall-clock, with no success gradient."
 where: Table 1 (p.5), Sec 5
 Fig 1 shows raw medians: clean $0.034 / 6 calls to $0.333 / 15 calls, a 9.9x raw median.
6. Unused branches are token-borne: ~1.9x cost with tool calls flat at 7 to 8, and no extra edits (association).
 quote: "runs with one unused branch have ≈1.9x the median cost of clean runs (n = 1,934 clean vs. 354 one-branch runs), while median tool calls change only from 7 to 8."
 where: Sec 5
7. Verbatim restatement of the task costs ~1.0x. Prompt length is not the driver; prompt content is.
 quote: "verbatim restatement of the task had approximately unit cost, indicating that prompt content rather than prompt length drives the observed effects in this setup."
 where: Sec 3, App E.1. Length-matched controls were 0.96-1.05x (App L).
 Mechanism: the user prompt is under 5% of input on PI.DEV and under 1% on Claude Code.
8. The bounded-efficiency template is neutral or better. It also has a failure mode on ambiguous specs.
 number: neutral on all 6 models; halves GLM-5.2 reasoning (0.48x); paraphrases 0.85-0.93x; ambiguous spec: 3/5 hidden-test failures vs 0/5 at baseline
 setup: In the Sonnet 5 follow-up (App M), the only Sonnet failures came from this wording, all on the ambiguous-spec task. The agent never read the in-repo requirements file.
 quote: "on an ambiguous specification, its stop-early framing reduced evidence seeking and produced 3/5 hidden-test failures versus 0/5 at baseline because the relevant in-repository requirements file was not consulted"
 where: Sec 4, App M
 Exact wording: "Work efficiently: begin with the failing test and the most likely implementation files; inspect additional files only when evidence requires it; avoid unrelated cleanup; make the smallest sufficient change; run the relevant tests; stop as soon as the acceptance criteria pass."
 Authors' advice (Sec 9): replace certainty demands with explicit verification and stopping rules, for example "running the relevant suite after the final edit and re-running it only after a relevant change or a failure". Require repo inspection when the spec is ambiguous.
9. Misleading hints are the costliest input defect and the only semantic marker linked to lower success.
 number: 2.61x reasoning; 4.2x pre-edit deliberation; rho=-0.19 for unsupported assumptions
 setup: Hint wording: "we believe the problem is caused by the test fixtures in tests/ ---start there." Ambiguous scope gave the lowest success in the benchmark (83%) with 1.44x reasoning. Irrelevant context was 1.03x. Conflicting constraints were 1.05x.
 where: Sec 4, App E.2
10. Cross-provider check on Claude Sonnet 5 (first-party API, 162 runs).
 number: multiple approaches 2.70x [2.14, 3.86] under PI.DEV and 2.52x [1.73, 3.48] under native Claude Code. max certainty 4.13x output tokens [1.42, 8.57] and 2.7x no-cache cost per success under Claude Code. deep thinking only 1.25-1.30x.
 setup: Metric is total-output-token ratio (thinking is billed inside output and not separable), so ratios are lower bounds on the effect on deliberation. The authors attribute the weak deep-thinking effect to the model's "adaptive-thinking controller" (an interpretation).
 where: App K
 Kimi-K3 replication (App J): multiple approaches 16.6x and deep thinking 14.8x, because its baseline is ~6x lower (55 vs 351/195 reasoning tokens). Absolute waste tokens are still at or below K2-generation levels.
11. Paraphrase robustness: all four paraphrase forms of multiple approaches, deep thinking and max certainty raised reasoning on every tested model (12/12 cells). Magnitude varies with form (3.0x concise to 6.7x verbose for multiple approaches). Position matters too (5.2x at start vs 4.3x at end). App L; 2,105 valid runs, 3 models.
12. Harness policy is the largest cost factor measured.
 number: 5-30x higher cost per success for Claude Code vs PI.DEV at ~equal success. 12-15x larger fixed prefix (15,983-20,330 vs 1,147-1,642 tokens). 2-7x more turns. 52% of Claude Code calls are test runs vs 22% on PI.DEV.
 setup: matched model/task/prompt; mostly open models via a LiteLLM gateway. Native Claude Code on Sonnet 5 was ~15x PI.DEV.
 quote: "Claude Code transmits a 12-15x larger fixed prefix than PI.DEV and uses 2-7x more turns, producing 5-30x higher cost per success at comparable success rates."
 where: Sec 6, App D, App K
 Prompt effects do not transfer across harnesses: goal-only prompts reduce reasoning under Claude Code (4/5 models), and exploration cues amplify 4-4.8x there vs 1.1-2.4x on PI.DEV (App E.3).
13. Harness x effort interaction (DeepSeek Harness, Sonnet 5).
 number: Effort-only cut cost 74.7% and the full stack 82.2%, vs ~19% and ~27% under Claude Code.
 setup: 5 tasks x 5 arms x 3 reps = 75 runs. All arms solved all 15 cells (ceiling tasks). The dsh baseline already ran aggressive reasoning by default, so effort control corrected an over-provisioned default. Mean cost per run: baseline $0.2753, effort $0.0696, full $0.0490.
 quote: "The result is a direct empirical interaction: the benefit of effort control depends on the harness default and request policy."
 where: Table 3, Sec 6.1, App O
14. More effort on hard tasks has model-dependent, often unfavorable returns (SWE-bench Verified hard slice, 25 instances, Claude Code, 150 paired cells).
 Opus 5 resolved 17/25 at low, 18/25 at high, 16/25 at xhigh (McNemar p=1.0). Cost per resolved task was $0.75, $1.89, $3.62.
 Sonnet 5 resolved 12/25 at low, 19/25 at high, 17/25 at xhigh. High vs low had 7 rescues and 0 regressions (p=0.016). Cost per resolved task was $1.76, $2.32, $3.00, so xhigh is dominated by high.
 xhigh vs low added 12-16k thinking tokens and 23-30 turns, with 2.4-4.5x billed cost. All 6 timeouts and 4 empty patches were at high or xhigh effort.
 Run-to-run noise is large: 6 of 10 discordant tasks were resolved by both settings on rerun.
 quote: "additional explicit effort has model-dependent and often unfavorable cost-success trade-offs."
 where: App N
 On easy deterministic tasks (App M), static maximum effort raised cost per success 1.5-2.8x, gained no successes and lost one. Effort controls did not reliably modulate compute on Together-served open models, so effort was not treated as an axis for them.
15. Caching cuts the bill without changing behavior.
 number: ~61% of the would-be bill cut on open models (billed cost ~39% of no-cache); 69-75% on the first-party Sonnet 5 API.
 quote: "billing reductions from caching should not be interpreted as behavioral efficiency gains."
 where: App E.4, App K

LIMITS (authors' own and what the paper does not show)
- Tasks are small (<=4 files) with high success ceilings; the paper states findings "may not transfer unchanged to long-horizon production agents". Absolute cost per run is tiny.
- The 1.9x, 18x, 2.4-7.4x and 5-30x figures are not SWE-bench effect sizes. The paper declines to extrapolate them to production workloads.
- Whether branching helps on architecture-dependent tasks is untested; the set has essentially none.
- Only the tested wordings are covered. Effects vary in size across paraphrase and position.
- Visible reasoning is not faithful or complete computation (Baherwani et al. 2026). Trace claims are about observable text only. Sonnet 5 is excluded from all trace-level claims.
- Judge reliability is modest. Same-model prompt sensitivity kappa=0.44. Cross-judge-model kappa=0.28 overall, 0.55-0.68 on the key fields. Hand labels agreed within +/-1 on 84.9% of fields.
- The mechanism-level cost associations (1.9x, 18x) are correlational, since annotated levels were not randomized. Tool-layer effects are directional only (zero-inflated counts).
- The "post-success" label rests on a visible-tests proxy.
- The dsh extension uses one closed model, 5 ceiling-success fixtures, and does not test DeepSeek models. The 82% is not a universal controller effect.
- The adaptive controller (Sec 8) is a proposal and is not evaluated.
- Cost uses pinned catalog prices. Provider classifier compute and latency are unmeasured.
- Dated: models and harness versions are fictional-future names (Claude Code 2.1.220, PI.DEV 0.82.1, Sonnet 5, Opus 5). Treat the numbers as tied to those versions.
- Authors are at PointFive, a cost-optimization company. This is a preprint, with preregistration claimed in the repo.

- LiteLLM v1.93.0; Together AI.
- Overthinking literature is mentioned only generically ("work on overthinking studies how much models deliberate"). No named paper or year is given.

CODE: none. The only load-bearing text is the prompt clauses quoted above. Table 4 (p.16) has the byte-exact frozen wording for all conditions.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.4), "Two waste mechanisms with different cost carriers". Bars show median no-cache cost by number of unused branches (cost ~1.9x, calls 7-8 flat) and by redundant-verification level (9.9x raw median, calls 6 to 15). It is the quickest way to show that reasoning overhead and tool-loop overhead are different waste, with success flat.
- Fig 2 (p.7), "Harness design changes both the agent trajectory and the value of control". Left, tool-call mix for Claude Code vs PI.DEV. Right, the same effort control saves 19%/27% under Claude Code but 75%/82% under dsh. It shows that an efficiency intervention's value is harness-conditional.
- Table 1 (p.5) gives the verification-severity gradient in numbers.

FIT WITH TARGET NOTE: 07-prompting-reasoning-models.md, overthinking/token-budget section. Use it for "do not ask for multiple approaches, extreme certainty or deep thinking by default; use explicit verification and stopping rules; bounded-efficiency wording is safe except when the spec is ambiguous". Use App N for effort budgets and the agent-prompting section for the harness caveat. It sharpens rather than contradicts the existing reasoning-model advice, so it needs a citation and a references row.

PROBLEMS: none in the extraction. The header text "[cs.CL]" is as printed. The SWE-bench appendix (N) and dsh extension (O) are described by the authors as post-registration and separate from the 4,644-run core benchmark. Their numbers should not be mixed with the core benchmark's. The paper states the scope of the 4,644 runs and 2,801 annotations itself (Sec 2). All Section 9 recommendations are the authors' interpretation, not directly measured outcomes (for example, the replacement verification-rule wording was not tested as its own arm).
